clue.text: Protector of a joint can keep members out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the two words before it are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A tin seems to shut away arms and legs, as if guarding a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the seven letters of CAN and KEEP. The surface reading of 'can keep members out' is a ban on club members.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the bone shield sitting over the front of the knee joint.

clue.text: Vessel said to be fine with fish in it

definitions.text: Vessel said to be fine with fish in it

parts.words: Vessel said to be fine with fish in it
parts.note: points to the idiom 'a fine ... of fish', a muddle, naming the pot in that saying

explanation.surface: A dish praised for holding a good catch.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'a pretty kettle of fish' names this boiling vessel.

clue.text: in black, according to O'Neill?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'in black, according to O'Neill?' starting lower-case: its opening words (the play title Mourning Becomes Electra) appear cut off by OCR, so the clue cannot be parsed as held

clue.text: Fickle sort, Cleo, involved with he-man

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so the letters of the two names are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Cleopatra-type flirt taking up with a muscleman, a changeable character.
explanation.definitionFit: A lizard that changes colour gives its name to a person who changes opinions to suit company.

clue.text: This jumper riders up!

parts.note: the jumper is not a sweater or a horse but a person who leaps from aircraft, and whose canopy carries them

explanation.surface: A sweater, or a showjumping horse, riding up on its wearer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who leaps from aircraft wearing a canopy is a skydiving jumper.

clue.text: Referee is a right snappy sort!

parts.note: someone who snaps with the teeth is a biter

explanation.surface: Calling the match official a proper grouch.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire or judge settling a dispute is a synonym for a referee.

clue.text: Brayer and Bumble's Law

definitions.meaning: a donkey is the animal that brays
Mr Bumble in Dickens's Oliver Twist declares that 'the law is a ...'

explanation.definitionFit: A donkey brays, and the beadle Bumble calls the law a foolish donkey in Oliver Twist.

clue.text: Not the sort of cheque to write with only one pound put away?

definitions.text: Not the sort of cheque to write with only one pound put away?

parts.words: Not the sort of cheque to write with only one pound put away?
parts.note: an unfilled cheque lets the payee name any sum, unwise with a single pound in the bank, and the pound sign L sits inside a bank

explanation.surface: Advice against signing an open cheque when your account holds a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque left without an amount filled in is an open, empty one.

clue.text: Oil changed after journey? Capital!

indicators.note: after places the rearranged oil behind the journey word

parts.note: a trip is a journey

indicators.note: changed means the letters of oil are put in a different order

explanation.surface: An oil change after a long drive, and the driver is delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' looks like an exclamation of approval after a motoring trip, but it is the definition, the Libyan city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Libyan seat of government on the Mediterranean is a capital city.

clue.text: Faction in split now settled

indicators.note: in places the word for a faction inside the word for a split

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split
a side is a faction in a dispute

explanation.surface: A breakaway group within a divided party has finally found peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living permanently in a place has settled there.

clue.text: Where's Roget? He's in The Bull!

indicators.note: in puts the letters of he's inside the sign's name

parts.note: Taurus is the zodiac sign of the Bull
taken as its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Asking where Mr Roget is and hearing he's at a pub called The Bull.
explanation.walkthrough: The pub reading of 'The Bull' hides the zodiac sign; 'Where's Roget?' asks where the compiler's name would be found.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Roget compiled the famous book of synonyms, so his name is found on its cover.

clue.text: What is wrong with a shot off-target?

parts.note: a shot that does not hit is a miss

explanation.surface: Asking what has gone wrong when a shot flies wide.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of order or faulty is wrong.

clue.text: Thing turning in a state of agitation, almost

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to be in a lather is to be agitated

explanation.surface: Something spinning while in a nervous fluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of LATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A workshop machine spins wood or metal against a cutting tool, so it is a turning thing.

clue.text: Broken-down car still has many revs in it

parts.note: a crock is a worn-out old vehicle
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: An old banger whose engine can still turn over fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Revs are revolutions of an engine in the surface, but Reverends here: Crockford's Clerical Directory lists the Church of England's clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Crockford's is the directory listing every Anglican clergyman, so many Reverends appear inside it.

clue.text: Strain Eliot suffered as a devotee of south-eastern Asia

indicators.note: suffered suggests the letters are put through rough treatment and come out rearranged

explanation.surface: T. S. Eliot's nerves gave way as he fell for the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar or lover of Eastern cultures and languages is a devotee of that region.

clue.text: An invalid, a true version of one?

definitions.text: An invalid, a true version of one?

indicators.note: a version is a different rendering, so the letters of the words before it are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Asking whether a sickly person is the genuine article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges AN INVALID A TRUE, all fourteen letters, and the whole clue describes the result: one obsessed with poor health.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypochondriac or chronically sickly person, anxious about health, is an invalid.

clue.text: Dry sort of car-dyer

parts.note: a stainer is one who dyes, and the clue invites reading the teetotaller as a kind of colourist

explanation.surface: A teetotal paint-shop worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller keeps off alcohol, so is dry.

clue.text: Declining to put advertisement in respectable environment

indicators.note: an environment surrounds, so the respectable word encloses the advertisement word

parts.note: decent means respectable

explanation.surface: Refusing to run an advert in a proper setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'environment' signals the surround; 'to put' only joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A society in moral decline is described as degenerate in that sense.

clue.text: Like a person in the country, thinking of new living-room?

definitions.text: Like a person in the country, thinking of new living-room?

parts.words: Like a person in the country, thinking of new living-room?
parts.note: the living-room is not a lounge but national territory, Lebensraum, wanted by a state bent on growth

explanation.surface: A country dweller planning a lounge extension.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation seeking more territory to live in pursues a policy of enlargement.

clue.text: Landlord opening his pub, perhaps, to advertise?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters may be arranged differently
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A publican launching his bar and wanting to spread the word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' takes the L of Landlord; 'perhaps' rearranges it with HIS and PUB.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something known publicly is to advertise it.

clue.text: Calls upon agent to provide king with endless venison, when ordered

indicators.note: when ordered says the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: endless cuts the final letter from the word

explanation.surface: An agent asked to supply the king with venison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims VENISON to VENISO, and 'when ordered' rearranges that with K.
explanation.definitionFit: To appeal to a god or a law is to call on it.

clue.text: Burns in trousers

definitions.meaning: bell-bottomed trousers widening at the ankle

explanation.definitionFit: A fire blazing up suddenly, and wide-legged bell-bottoms, share one word.

clue.text: Showy trailer a beaut going around Rhode Island

indicators.note: around wraps the shuffled letters about the state abbreviation
going means the letters move away from their order

parts.note: taken as written, A BEAUT, with the extra I the setter's fodder needed to give nine letters
RI is the abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A lovely caravan towed round a small American state.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed fodder is one I short: AUBRIETIA needs A BEAUT plus another I around RI. 'going' rearranges the fodder and 'around' wraps it round RI.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailing rock plant with bright purple flowers is a showy creeper.

clue.text: Bury, in the off-season, employs no women

indicators.note: no means the letter for women is removed

parts.note: winter is the off-season for many resorts

explanation.surface: A Lancashire town with no female staff out of season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no women' drops the W. Bury is a town in Lancashire as well as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To place a body in a grave is to bury it.

clue.text: Forger's block

parts.note: a forger here is a smith who shapes hot metal, and the block is the iron he hammers on, not a mental block of a counterfeiter

explanation.definitionFit: A smith hammers hot iron on a heavy steel block.

clue.text: Live and die, say, around the south

indicators.note: around wraps the word for death about the south letter

parts.note: an exit is a death, as in a stage exit for a character
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Life and death in the southern hemisphere.
explanation.definitionFit: To be alive is to be.

clue.text: Sail with a king in a bowler?

indicators.note: in places the two pieces inside the bowler word

parts.note: a spinner is a type of cricket bowler who spins the ball
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch wearing a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The bowler is not a hat but a cricket bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A large balloon-shaped sail flown at a yacht's bow downwind is a sail.

clue.text: Sunday popular for crime?

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A trendy Sunday for wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: A transgression against moral law is a wrongdoing like a crime.

clue.text: What could become the Near Eastern capital?

indicators.note: could become shows the letters may be turned into something else, a new order

explanation.surface: A question about the Near East's chief city.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran's chief city is an Eastern seat of government.

clue.text: Half of this corrodes and jams

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters

parts.note: rusts means corrodes

explanation.surface: Something partly corroding and seizing up.
explanation.definitionFit: To jam something in is to shove or push it hard.
